direct_answer:
Yes. OMV states that it "has developed a transition plan" to support its ambition of becoming a net-zero business by 2050 and that the plan is an integral part of OMV Strategy 2030, complemented by short-, mid-, and long-term targets (including net zero Scopes 1–3 by 2050; Scope 1–2 absolute reductions of 30% by 2030 and 60% by 2040; and Scope 3 absolute reductions of 20% by 2030 and 50% by 2040 for defined categories) [Source 2].

On alignment with limiting warming to 1.5°C: OMV reports that it assessed alignment of its climate targets with a 1.5°C world using IPCC 1.5°C (no/limited overshoot) scenarios and IEA WEO 2024 scenarios (including NZE, described as corresponding to 1.5°C), and concludes that "All OMV's targets fall within this range, indicating alignment with a 1.5°C world"; it also states its 2030 Scope 3 target is "very close" to the IEA NZE pathway [Source 6]. OMV further concludes that its targets are aligned with the Paris Agreement goal of "well below 2°C" and that it is "confident" its Scope 3 2030 targets are compatible with limiting warming to 1.5°C, while Scope 1 and 2 targets "come close" [Source 1]. Therefore, OMV presents its transition plan/targets as (at least) within range/near-aligned with 1.5°C, with some nuance by scope [Sources 1, 6].

A timeline for adopting a transition plan is not applicable because OMV discloses that it already has a transition plan [Source 2].
compliance_rationale: Evidence confirms existence of a climate mitigation transition plan and provides key elements (integration into Strategy 2030, net-zero-by-2050 ambition, and interim Scope 1–3 targets) [Source 2]. Evidence also addresses 1.5°C compatibility through scenario-based assessment referencing IPCC 1.5°C scenarios and IEA NZE (1.5°C) and provides OMV’s stated conclusion on alignment/near-alignment (including nuance across scopes) [Sources 1, 6]. However, the retrieved passages do not provide all ESRS E1-4.34(e) elements (e.g., whether targets are science-based, the specific framework/methodology used beyond scenario references, underlying policy assumptions in detail, and whether targets have been externally assured).
disclosure_gaps: Whether and how OMV’s GHG targets are formally science-based (e.g., SBTi or other science-based framework) is not evidenced in the retrieved passages (beyond scenario comparisons) (ESRS E1-4.34(e)).
External assurance/verification status of the GHG targets (or the 1.5°C alignment assessment) is not evidenced in the retrieved passages (ESRS E1-4.34(e)).

Detailed description of the framework/methodology used to assess 1.5°C compatibility (beyond high-level IPCC/IEA scenario use and outlier trimming) is not fully evidenced (ESRS E1-4.34(e)) [Source 6].

Underlying climate and policy scenario assumptions used for targets (beyond naming IPCC 1.5°C scenarios and IEA WEO scenarios) are not fully evidenced in the retrieved passages (ESRS E1-4.34(e)) [Source 6].
key_findings: OMV discloses it has a climate change mitigation transition plan integrated into OMV Strategy 2030, with targets toward net zero Scopes 1–3 by 2050 [Source 2].

OMV’s interim targets include: Scope 1–2 absolute reductions of 30% by 2030 and 60% by 2040; Scope 3 (defined categories) absolute reductions of 20% by 2030 and 50% by 2040; and carbon-intensity decline targets for energy supply [Source 2].

OMV assessed 1.5°C alignment using IPCC 1.5°C (no/limited overshoot) scenarios and IEA WEO 2024 scenarios (including NZE) and states its targets fall within the 1.5°C scenario range; it also states its 2030 Scope 3 target is very close to the IEA NZE pathway [Source 6].

OMV concludes its targets are aligned with Paris Agreement 'well below 2°C' and expresses confidence that Scope 3 2030 targets are compatible with 1.5°C, while Scope 1 and 2 targets 'come close' [Source 1].
